items.title: 66960_Gil Evans oral history interview
items.q: My first step-father was, his name was Gustin and they lived in Florida.

ctx.x: And I think that they were very colorful apparently to you or for you and I think they would be for people who are going to be listening to this in years to come. I'm wondering if you might want to talk about some of the very colorful mining camps or lumber camps. Or any of the places at which you spent your time.

I was very young at the time. I don't remember it too well. I only have impressions you know. We lived in Florida for a while. My mother was remarried in Florida. My first step-father was, his name was Gustin and they lived in Florida. My mother ran a little hotel on a road between two towns. I can't remember which, what the

name of the towns were and I think it was Lake Worth and some other town. And in those days it was still pretty wild down there. Because that was around 1918. I can remember at night waking up and hearing the wild horses running by.
